City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
March 5, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:02 p.m. , on March 5, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on February 29, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ury
INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the City and Cityâ??s Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council received information and provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action from Closed Session.
PRESENTATIONS
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Wendy Burge-Dickinson, M.V.: announced that Jersey Mike’s is hosting a Military Outreach Fundraiser from Friday, March 16 through Sunday March 18, 2012. That weekend, Jersey Mike’s will donate 20% of all proceeds to Words of Comfort, Hope and Promise.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that the owner/developer of the former K-Mart property should not be let out of its obligation to provide affordable housing.
Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V.: speaking as the City’s liaison from Casta del Sol, she introduced the new General Manager of Casta del Sol, Josh Hodosh.
Michael Muno, M.V.: discussed a claim that he filed with the City (agenda item 5) and stated that he is concerned for his family’s safety. He requested that a tree on the slope behind his home be removed immediately.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 5 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of February 20, 2012, as presented.
3.
Check Register dated February 10, 2012 in the amount of $862,116.58
Ratified the accompanying check register.
4.
Check Register dated February 17, 2012 in the amount of $807,006.95
Ratified the accompanying check register.
6.
2012 CDBG Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)
(1) Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to R.J. Noble Company in the amount of $336,685.00; and (2) adopted Resolution 12-13 Amending the FY 11/12 Budget to Recognize CDBG Revenue Available for Residential Street Resurfacing Project (CIP 838) and an Offsetting Appropriation to Utilize These Funds.
7.
Oso/Marguerite Intersection Improvements (CIP 844) and Oso Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 205)
(1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject projects; (2) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; (4) authorized payment of the final retention; and (5) authorized payment of $4,500 to each of the 29 affected property owners along Pinario and Monforte, per the approval action of Resolution 05-51.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
Item 5 was taken out of order.
5.
Claim Against the City - Michael Muno
City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.
The Council Members asked questions of staff.
Michael Muno, M.V.: stated that the trees on the slope behind his home had not been watered for two years. He noted that the tree was cut down the day after its branch fell and broke his fence and a new watering system has since been installed.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Ury, to deny the claim.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
None
PUBLIC HEARINGS
8.
Proposed Ordinance designating Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones within the City of Mission Viejo as recommended by the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection. The proposed Ordinance will impact several areas along the City’s eastern boundary, and areas northerly of the Foothill Transportation Corridor (SR 241) and in vicinity of El Toro Road
City Attorney Bill Curley explained why Mayor Ury and Council Member Leckness should not participate in the discussion of this item. He noted that Mayor Ury’s home is very close to one of the affected High Fire Hazard Zones and Council Member Leckness’ home is inside the Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone. Mr. Curley recommended that they recuse themselves from the discussion and vote.
At the hour of 6:31 p.m., Mayor Ury turned the meeting over to Mayor Pro Tem Reardon and he and Council Member Leckness left the room.
Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.
Fire Marshal Laura Blaul, OCFA: presented an overview of the purpose of the Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone Maps and the legal requirements behind the map updates.
At the hour of 7:08 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon opened the public hearing.
The following spoke in opposition to the proposed Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone Maps: Gail Reavis, M.V.; Joe Holtzman, M.V.; Greg Woodard, M.V.; Robert Luher, Board Member of the Canyon Estates Community Association, M.V.; John Cussen, Community Manager of the Cordova Homeowners Association, M.V.; Joel Sugg, M.V.; Claire Kretzmer, M.V.; Joann Bullington, M.V.; Mark Sayler, M.V.; Ramsey Azzouni, M.V.; Lisa Rivier, M.V.; Kime Goodrum, M.V.; Eric R. Chambers, M.V.; and Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.
Greg Woodard submitted a petition signed by approximately 200 Painted Trails residents who are opposed to the maps.
The following presented written comments in opposition to the proposed maps: Andrew Potter, M.V. and Timothy E. Riddle, M.V.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that the City Council received written/email correspondence in opposition to the maps from the following residents, prior to the Council Meeting: Carroll S. Slemaker, M.V.; Derik and Kristen Van Leeuwen, M.V.; and Rick Lustig, M.V.
Fire Marshal Blaul responded to questions that were raised during the public hearing.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
RECESS
At the hour of 8:48 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:59 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
OLD BUSINESS
NEW BUSINESS
MAYO'RS, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
9.
Mayor’s Selection and Appointment of Two Members to the Oversight Board Pursuant to California Health and Safety Code, Division 24, Part 1.85, Section 34179
Mayor Ury appointed himself and City Treasurer Cheryl Dyas to the Oversight Board Pursuant to California Health and Safety Code, Division 24, Part 1.85, Section 34179.
10.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
11.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury presented the report.
12.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin Hills TCA however she has a meeting this week.
13.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager's Report
City Attorney's Report
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
14.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley reminded the public of the Farmers Market every Friday from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at the Civic Center. She encouraged residents to visit and noted that there are many great choices and all the produce is fresh. Council Member Kelley announced that she has been out of town so she missed some of the fun events this last week but she is glad to be back.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness outlined his attendance at the grand opening of Global Tile and Stone on Via Fabricante as well as the Little League grand opening last weekend. He also enjoyed watching the electric jets at Up in the Air and he stated that it was another fantastic event.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht discussed her attendance at the Little League Opening Ceremonies and she thanked the coaches and parents for their time and dedication to the children. She announced that the Diablos and Cougars basketball teams have made the state playoff championships and she encouraged residents to check MissionViejoDispatch.com for locations and times. Council Member Schlicht outlined her attendance at various events including the Saddleback Valley American Legion’s ceremony honoring South County’s law enforcement personnel, Up in the Air, and the Mission Viejo Elks Ladies 8th Annual Fashion Show. She announced that the voters killed the El Toro Airport 10 years ago today and she thanked anti-airport supporter Gail Reavis for her hard work and effort. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from Patrick Henry: “The liberties of a people never were, nor ever will be, secure, when the transactions of their rulers may be concealed from them.”
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she participated in the Read Across America event by reading “Duck for President” to three separate groups of first graders at Castille Elementary School. She found it interesting to try and explain the role of a Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem to the youngsters and she said she had a lot of fun. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon also attended the Up in the Air event with her grandson and she visited four of the Little League Grand Opening ceremonies. Finally, she announced that she will be volunteering this year at the Tee it up Fore Marines Golf Tournament and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon thanked staff for their help with the public hearing earlier in the evening.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury announced that he too attended the Little League Opening Day Ceremonies. He appreciated the hospitality and he thanked the coaches and the parents for their hard work. Mayor Ury announced that the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce will be hosting its annual Chamber Breakfast on March 29, 2012, at 7:30 a.m. at the Mission Viejo Country Club.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 9:13 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, March 19, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of March 19, 2012
